verses.english: 4. The Host of a Hundred Felicities

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

verses.pali: Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
verses.english: Then, late at night, several glorious deities of the host of a hundred felicities, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
verses.english: Standing to one side, one deity spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

verses.pali: Yaso ca kittī ca tatvassa hoti,

verses.english: and when they discard this corpse they go to heaven.”

verses.pali: Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
verses.english: Then another deity recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“Give up anger, get rid of conceit,
and get past all the fetters.
Chains don’t torment one who has nothing,
not clinging to name and form.”
For if you’re diligent and practice absorption,
